letter.p1: My name is Luis Aníbal García, Founder and Technical Director of Panamerican Dojo Kai USA and Venezuela. I received my first black belt from the United States Karate Association in 1979 and hold a 7th Dan title awarded in 2009. I trained under the esteemed Japanese Shihan Kasuhiko Morita, maintaining a lasting bond with Japan Karatedo Dojokai, our main headquarters in Japan.
letter.p2: Our dojos have always been places where family, humanity, and discipline prevail, promoting strong values and teaching traditional karate-do as a method of self-defense without inciting violence, upholding humility, and remaining apart from commercial trends.
letter.p3: We are honored to share that, for the first time, dojos from the USA and Venezuela have been formally invited to participate in the 51st All-Japan Karate-do Dojokai Championship, to be held on November 3, 2025, in Tachikawa City, Tokyo. This unique opportunity offers cultural exchange, international competition, and personal growth for our athletes.
letter.p4: As with many international events, the costs involved—including travel, lodging, tournament fees, meals, and training—are significant and must be covered by the families and dojo community.
letter.p5: We respectfully invite you to consider sponsoring our delegation. Any support will be gratefully received. Your sponsorship would directly empower our youth to represent both the USA and Venezuela on a world stage, while also showcasing your commitment to youth development, cultural exchange, and wellness through sport. All contributions, regardless of amount, will make a meaningful difference for our athletes.
